item.title: Canadian Poet Anne Carson Is Awarded Nobel Prize in Literature
item.description: The writer joins a list of laureates that includes Toni Morrison, Samuel Beckett and Bob Dylan.
item.dc:creator: Alex Marshall
item.media:credit: Rob Bennett for The New York Times
item.media:description: Anne Carson at a reading in New York in 2008.

item.title: Hiker, 16, Is Rescued From ‘Widowmaker’ Ledge After Using Chatbot to Plan Route
item.description: Bryce Vincent Gowryluk used Claude, Anthropic’s A.I. chatbot, to help him chart a course for the top of Crown Mountain, north of Vancouver, British Columbia. Things did not go as planned.
item.dc:creator: Michael Levenson

item.title: Canada Halts Plan to Allow Medically Assisted Death for the Mentally Ill
item.description: People who have mental illness alone will not qualify for assisted death, but patients who have other conditions and expect to have a cognitive decline can make an advanced request.
item.dc:creator: Vjosa Isai
item.media:description: Sean Fraser, Canada’s minister of justice, said parliament will pass legislation to bar people whose sole condition is a mental illness from seeking medically assisted death.

item.title: Man Posing as ICE Agent at Miami Polling Site Faces Felony Charges
item.description: Danilo Alves Silva wore an Immigration and Customs Enforcement costume from Amazon at a polling location for the Brazilian presidential election.
item.dc:creator: Laura Chung and Remy Tumin
item.media:description: The Kendall campus of Miami Dade College in Florida, where Brazilian nationals voted in their country’s presidential election.

item.title: Mass Trials Put Hundreds in One Dock in El Salvador
item.description: Lawyers warn that the mass trials of people imprisoned during President Nayib Bukele’s gang crackdown are marred by vague evidence and restrictions on a proper defense.
item.dc:creator: James Wagner
item.category: Human Rights and Human Rights Violations
item.media:description: Inmates during a mass hearing at the Terrorism Confinement Center, or CECOT, prison in April in Tecoluca, El Salvador.

item.title: Can Artificial Intelligence Learn the Art of Surgery?
item.description: Canada wants to leverage A.I. to improve its health care system. At a Toronto hospital, surgeons are training a machine to distinguish a safe incision from a catastrophic one.
item.dc:creator: Vjosa Isai and Cole Burston
item.media:credit: Cole Burston for The New York Times
item.media:description: Dr. Madani, left, and Dr. Timothy Jackson, perform laparoscopic cholecystectomy surgery on a patient at Toronto General Hospital, with the help of visual A.I. guides.

item.title: Tropical Storm Isaias Could Become the First Atlantic Hurricane of the Year
item.description: The storm will move north toward the Gulf Coast of the United States over the next few days, forecasters said.
item.dc:creator: Nazaneen Ghaffar

item.title: F.B.I. Charges American in Plot Behind Canada’s Tumbler Ridge School Shooting
item.description: The U.S. police say a 30-year-old offered the killer advice and cash for supplies at least six months before the rampage in British Columbia that left eight dead.
item.dc:creator: Vjosa Isai
item.media:credit: Alana Paterson for The New York Times
item.media:description: A memorial for the victims of the mass shooting at Tumbler Ridge Secondary School in British Columbia, in February.

item.title: Bolsonaro Family Emerges Triumphant in Brazil’s Elections, Mounting a Surprising Resurrection
item.description: The Bolsonaro family emerged triumphant in Brazil’s elections, mounting a surprising political resurrection in Latin America’s largest nation.
item.dc:creator: Ana Ionova
item.media:description: The presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro in Brasília on Sunday.

item.title: U.S. Sends Reaper Drones to Colombia and Ecuador to Hunt Cartels
item.description: MQ-9 Reaper drones — known for high-profile deadly strikes — have been shifted from Africa to Colombia and Ecuador, U.S. officials said.
item.dc:creator: Annie Correal and Eric Schmitt
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: An MQ-9 Reaper drone at Hancock Field Air National Guard base near Syracuse, N.Y.

item.title: The Separatist Parti Québécois Wins Quebec Election, Reviving Sovereignty Push
item.description: The separatist party’s victory fell short of clinching a majority that would have all but guaranteed a potential showdown with Ottawa over Canada’s future.
item.dc:creator: Norimitsu Onishi
item.media:description: Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, the leader of the Parti Québécois, celebrated a provincial election victory in Montreal.

item.title: Brazil Election Could Give Bolsonaro a Key Role in Trump’s Latin America Map
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, now the favorite to win Brazil’s presidency, would give President Trump a critical new ally in Latin America, particularly on security.
item.dc:creator: Jack Nicas
item.media:description: An effigy of President Trump carrying a depiction of an incarcerated President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva during a rally in São Paulo last month in support of Flávio Bolsonaro, the right-wing opposition candidate.

item.title: In a Major Boost for the Right, Another Bolsonaro Nears Brazil’s Presidency
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro’s first round lead leaves President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva three weeks to find the votes to stop Brazil’s, and Latin America’s, rightward shift.
item.dc:creator: Ana Ionova and Adam B. Ellick
item.media:description: Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of Brazil’s former president Jair Bolsonaro, had the lead after Sunday’s vote.

item.title: Voters in Quebec Election Go to Polls as Separatist Parti Québécois Leads
item.description: The Parti Québécois, which promised an independence referendum if elected on Monday, could return to power after more than a decade.
item.dc:creator: Norimitsu Onishi
item.media:description: Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, the leader of the separatist Parti Québécois, arriving to cast his ballot on Monday during Quebec’s provincial election in Montreal.

item.title: Brazil Elections Head to Runoff Between Lula and Bolsonaro
item.description: Neither President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva nor Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of a former president, won the first round, but Mr. Bolsonaro took more votes.
item.dc:creator: Ana Ionova and Adam B. Ellick

item.title: Peppino Mazzullo, Voice of Topo Gigio For Decades, Dies at 100
item.description: The actor played the role of the sweetly endearing mouse puppet, a character beloved by children all over the world — and, apparently, Ed Sullivan.
item.dc:creator: Kaja Andric
item.media:credit: Mario Notarangelo Mondadori Portfolio, via Getty Images
item.media:description: Mr. Mazzullo in the 1970s with Topo Gigio and the puppet’s designer, Maria Perego.

item.title: Overlooked No More: Eugenia Errázuriz, Who Opened Doors for Picasso
item.description: She moved from Chile to Paris, where she used her wealth to support Picasso, Stravinsky and other artists. World War II forced her to go home, where she ended her life.
item.dc:creator: Penelope Rowlands

item.title: Understanding Canada’s Europe Pivot
item.description: You sent us your questions about the prime minister’s plan to form a closer relationship with the European Union. Our Canada bureau chief answers them.
item.dc:creator: Matina Stevis-Gridneff
item.media:description: Prime Minister Mark Carney at the European Parliament in Strasbourg, France, on Sept. 17.

item.title: These Birds Are Louder Than Elephants, Jackhammers and Chain Saws
item.description: A new study has identified two species of Brazilian birds, the bare-throated bellbird and the red-legged seriema, as the loudest in nature.
item.dc:creator: Taylor Mitchell Brown

item.title: Separatists Are Poised to Win Quebec’s Election. Independence Is Still a Hard Sell.
item.description: The Parti Québécois has vowed to hold a referendum on independence, three decades after Quebec voted “no.” Voters want change, but maybe not that much.

item.media:credit: Renaud Philippe for The New York Times
item.media:description: Supporters at the Québec Solidaire campaign office in Jean-Lesage watch Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, the leader of the Parti Québécois, during the leaders’ debate last month.

item.title: What We Learned About American Teenagers Supplying Guns to Cartels

item.media:description: Two teenage American weapons traffickers known as El Flaco, left, and Chuy, in the desert outside Phoenix, where they shot rifles.

item.title: F.D.A. Found Cyclospora During Taylor Farms Inspection in Mexico
item.description: The discovery adds strong evidence that the outbreak that sickened thousands over the summer originated in a grower’s field or processing facility.
item.dc:creator: Christina Jewett, Alice Callahan and Caroline Hopkins Legaspi
item.media:credit: Fred Ramos for The New York Times
item.media:description: Over the course of the summer, the cyclospora outbreak linked to Taylor Farms caused nearly 13,000 illnesses, 570 hospitalizations and two deaths in 21 states.

item.title: Argentina’s ‘Golden Passport’ Program Offers Citizenship in Exchange for Foreign Cash
item.description: The program would grant citizenship to people who make major investments in Argentina. Similar efforts have yielded significant income for small economies, but have also led to risks.
item.dc:creator: Emma Bubola
item.media:credit: Victor Moriyama for The New York Times
item.media:description: President Javier Milei of Argentina in July.

item.title: Why U.S. Diesel Is So Important to Major Trading Partners
item.description: Economies in Latin America and Europe rely on American diesel. Stopping exports could tip some countries into recession, hurting trade with the United States.
item.dc:creator: Simon Romero
item.media:description: Adjusting the price of gasoline in Pôrto Alegre, Brazil, this year.

item.title: Coast Guard Says It Stopped Ships Carrying Fuel to Cuba
item.description: The Coast Guard has intercepted two small boats it says were carrying illegal fuel to Cuba as the United States enforces a fuel blockade aimed at Cuba’s Communist government.
item.dc:creator: David C. Adams
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: “The high seas are not a sanctuary for lawlessness,” Coast Guard Commandant Admiral Kevin Lunday, said of the seizure of boats.

item.title: U.S. Suspends Consular Services in Brazil on Eve of Elections
item.description: The State Department cited unspecified security concerns in announcing the unusual move. A closely fought presidential election in Brazil takes place on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Claire Moses
item.media:description: The U.S. Consulate in Rio de Janeiro.

item.title: Mike Smith, Bubbles on ‘Trailer Park Boys,’ Has Sexual Assault Charge Dismissed
item.description: The Canadian cult comedy series announced that Mr. Smith, 54, would resume his involvement with the show.
item.dc:creator: Neil Vigdor
item.media:description: Mike Smith in 2014. A sexual assault charge against Mr. Smith, who plays Bubbles in the Canadian mockumentary series “Trailer Park Boys,” was dismissed on Thursday. He had pleaded not guilty.

item.title: Canada’s Proposed Oil Pipeline Offers Carney Relief From Domestic and Global Turmoil
item.description: The new pipeline from Alberta’s oil sands to the Pacific Coast may lower separatist tensions in that province while also loosening energy ties with the U.S.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen
item.category: Far East, South and Southeast Asia and Pacific Areas
item.media:description: Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada speaking about an oil pipeline planned to connect distribution points in Alberta to ports in British Columbia on Thursday in Fort McMurray, Alberta.
